claim: White adipose tissue (WAT) remodeling is dictated by coordinated interactions between adipocytes and resident stromal-vascular cells.
source: White adipose tissue (WAT) remodeling is dictated by coordinated interactions between adipocytes and resident stromal-vascular cells; however, the functional heterogeneity of adipose stromal cells has remained unresolved.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific understanding about WAT remodeling, presented as background knowledge in the abstract.

claim: The functional heterogeneity of adipose stromal cells has remained unresolved.
source: White adipose tissue (WAT) remodeling is dictated by coordinated interactions between adipocytes and resident stromal-vascular cells; however, the functional heterogeneity of adipose stromal cells has remained unresolved.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing and FACS were combined to identify and isolate functionally distinct subpopulations of PDGFRβ+ stromal cells within visceral WAT of adult mice.
source: We combined single-cell RNA-sequencing and FACS to identify and isolate functionally distinct subpopulations of PDGFRβ+ stromal cells within visceral WAT of adult mice.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells represent highly adipogenic visceral adipocyte precursor cells ('APCs').
source: LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells represent highly adipogenic visceral adipocyte precursor cells ('APCs'), whereas LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells represent fibro-inflammatory progenitors ('FIPs').
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data including differentiation assays and gene expression analysis.

claim: LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells represent fibro-inflammatory progenitors ('FIPs').
source: LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells represent highly adipogenic visceral adipocyte precursor cells ('APCs'), whereas LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells represent fibro-inflammatory progenitors ('FIPs').
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data including gene expression profiling and functional assays.

claim: FIPs lack adipogenic capacity.
source: FIPs lack adipogenic capacity, display pro-fibrogenic/pro-inflammatory phenotypes, and can exert an anti-adipogenic effect on APCs.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro differentiation assays showing FIPs do not spontaneously differentiate into adipocytes.

claim: FIPs display pro-fibrogenic/pro-inflammatory phenotypes.
source: FIPs lack adipogenic capacity, display pro-fibrogenic/pro-inflammatory phenotypes, and can exert an anti-adipogenic effect on APCs.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis showing enrichment of fibrogenic and inflammatory genes, and functional assays demonstrating inflammatory responses.

claim: FIPs can exert an anti-adipogenic effect on APCs.
source: FIPs lack adipogenic capacity, display pro-fibrogenic/pro-inflammatory phenotypes, and can exert an anti-adipogenic effect on APCs.
evidence: This is supported by conditioned media experiments showing that media from FIPs inhibits adipocyte differentiation of APCs.

claim: The pro-inflammatory phenotype of PDGFRβ+ cells is regulated, at least in part, by NR4A nuclear receptors.
source: The pro-inflammatory phenotype of PDGFRβ+ cells is regulated, at least in part, by NR4A nuclear receptors.
evidence: This is supported by gain- and loss-of-function experiments showing that NR4A family members modulate inflammatory cytokine expression in FIPs.

claim: WAT is composed of energy-storing adipocytes, various immune cell populations, vascular cells, adipocyte precursor cells (APCs), and largely uncharacterized stromal populations.
source: WAT is composed of energy-storing adipocytes, various immune cell populations, vascular cells, adipocyte precursor cells (APCs), and largely uncharacterized stromal populations.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about WAT composition.

claim: The development and function of adipose tissue is highly dependent on critical interactions between adipocytes, APCs, immune cells, and endothelial cells.
source: The development and function of adipose tissue is highly dependent on critical interactions between adipocytes, APCs, immune cells, and endothelial cells (Han et al., 2011; Hong et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: WAT has a unique and remarkable capacity to expand and contract in size in response to changes in demand for energy storage.
source: WAT has a unique and remarkable capacity to expand and contract in size in response to changes in demand for energy storage.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about WAT plasticity.

claim: Individuals who preferentially accumulate WAT in subcutaneous regions are at a relatively lower risk for developing insulin resistance when compared to equally obese individuals with central (visceral) adiposity.
source: It has long been appreciated that individuals who preferentially accumulate WAT in subcutaneous regions are at a relatively lower risk for developing insulin resistance when compared to equally obese individuals with central (visceral) adiposity (Kissebah et al., 1982; Krotkiewski et al., 1983).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Visceral and subcutaneous WAT depots represent fundamentally distinct types of WAT.
source: It is now widely believed that visceral and subcutaneous WAT depots represent fundamentally distinct types of WAT (Karastergiou et al., 2013; Lee et al., 2013; Macotela et al., 2012; Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Visceral and subcutaneous WAT depots emanate from distinct developmental lineages.
source: Indeed, visceral and subcutaneous WAT depots emanate from distinct developmental lineages (Chau et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The manner in which individual WAT depots expand and 'remodel' is a clear determinant of metabolic health in obesity.
source: Importantly, another clear determinant of metabolic health in obesity is manner in which individual WAT depots expand and 'remodel' (Hepler and Gupta, 2017; Lee et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Pathological WAT expansion is characterized by the presence of enlarged adipocytes, excessive macrophage accumulation, and fibrosis.
source: Pathological WAT expansion is characterized by the presence of enlarged adipocytes, excessive macrophage accumulation, and fibrosis (Divoux et al., 2010; Gustafson et al., 2009; Hardy et al., 2011; Klöting and Blüher, 2014; Sun et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Healthy WAT expansion occurs when adipose tissue expands through adipocyte hyperplasia (increase in adipocyte number through de novo differentiation).
source: Healthy WAT expansion occurs when adipose tissue expands through adipocyte hyperplasia (increase in adipocyte number through de novo differentiation) (Denis and Obin, 2013; Kim et al., 2014; Klöting et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Healthy WAT expansion is associated with a lower degree of chronic tissue inflammation and fibrosis.
source: This is associated with a lower degree of chronic tissue inflammation and fibrosis.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge in the context of healthy WAT expansion.

claim: The epididymal WAT depot expands through both adipocyte hypertrophy and adipocyte hyperplasia in male C57BL/6 mice during diet-induced obesity.
source: The epididymal WAT depot expands through both adipocyte hypertrophy and adipocyte hyperplasia (Jeffery et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2013b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The inguinal subcutaneous WAT depot expands almost exclusively by adipocyte hypertrophy in male C57BL/6 mice during diet-induced obesity.
source: The inguinal subcutaneous WAT depot expands almost exclusively by adipocyte hypertrophy.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about depot-specific expansion patterns.

claim: Visceral adipocytes emerging in association with HFD feeding originate, at least in part, from perivascular precursors expressing Pdgfrb.
source: We recently reported that visceral adipocytes emerging in association with HFD feeding originate, at least in part, from perivascular precursors expressing Pdgfrb (Vishvanath et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Pdgfrb encodes the platelet-derived growth factor receptor β chain (PDGFRβ protein) and is a widely used marker of perivascular cells.
source: Pdgfrb encodes the platelet-derived growth factor receptor β chain (PDGFRβ protein) and is a widely used marker of perivascular cells (Armulik et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Following HFD feeding, Pdgfrb-expressing cells give rise to white adipocytes within visceral WAT depots.
source: Following HFD feeding, Pdgfrb-expressing cells give rise to white adipocytes within visceral WAT depots (Vishvanath et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work using lineage tracing.

claim: The ability of Pdgfrb-expressing precursors to undergo de novo adipogenesis in the setting of diet-induced obesity is critical for healthy visceral WAT expansion.
source: The ability of these precursors to undergo de novo adipogenesis in the setting of diet-induced obesity is critical for healthy visceral WAT expansion (Shao et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Inducible genetic disruption of Pparg in Pdgfrb-expressing cells leads to a loss of de novo adipogenesis from Pdgfrb-expressing cells in the visceral WAT depot of diet-induced obese mice.
source: Inducible genetic disruption of Pparg, the master regulatory gene of adipocyte differentiation, in Pdgfrb-expressing cells leads to a loss of de novo adipogenesis from Pdgfrb-expressing cells in the visceral WAT depot of diet-induced obese mice; this exacerbates the pathologic remodeling of this depot (i.e. increased inflammation and fibrosis).
evidence: This statement describes experimental findings from the authors' previous work.

claim: Driving de novo adipogenesis from Pdgfrb-expressing cells through transgenic Pparg expression leads to a healthy expansion of visceral WAT (lower inflammation and small adipocytes).
source: Driving de novo adipogenesis from Pdgfrb-expressing cells through transgenic Pparg expression leads to a healthy expansion of visceral WAT (lower inflammation and small adipocytes) (Shao et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The highly adipogenic subpopulation of PDGFRβ+ cells in gonadal WAT (gWAT) is quantitatively enriched in the expression of Pparg and Zfp423.
source: The highly adipogenic subpopulation of PDGFRβ+ cells in gonadal WAT (gWAT) is quantitatively enriched in the expression of Pparg, as well as its upstream regulatory factor, Zfp423 (Gupta et al., 2012; Tang et al., 2008; Vishvanath et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PDGFRβ+ cells enriched in adipogenic factors express several mural cell (pericyte/smooth muscle) markers and reside directly adjacent to the endothelium in WAT blood vessels.
source: PDGFRβ+ cells enriched in these adipogenic factors express several mural cell (pericyte/smooth muscle) markers and reside directly adjacent to the endothelium in WAT blood vessels (Gupta et al., 2012; Tang et al., 2008; Vishvanath et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PDGFRβ+ cells expressing high levels of Zfp423 (GFP+ or Zfp423High) represent highly committed preadipocytes.
source: Using Zfp423 reporter mice (Zfp423GFP BAC transgenic mice), we revealed that PDGFRβ+ cells expressing high levels of Zfp423 (GFP+ or Zfp423High) represent highly committed preadipocytes while Zfp423Low cells (GFP-) lacked significant adipogenic capacity, and exhibited significantly different global patterns of gene expression (Vishvanath et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Zfp423Low PDGFRβ+ cells (GFP-) lack significant adipogenic capacity.
source: Using Zfp423 reporter mice (Zfp423GFP BAC transgenic mice), we revealed that PDGFRβ+ cells expressing high levels of Zfp423 (GFP+ or Zfp423High) represent highly committed preadipocytes while Zfp423Low cells (GFP-) lacked significant adipogenic capacity, and exhibited significantly different global patterns of gene expression (Vishvanath et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Zfp423High and Zfp423Low PDGFRβ+ cells exhibit significantly different global patterns of gene expression.
source: Using Zfp423 reporter mice (Zfp423GFP BAC transgenic mice), we revealed that PDGFRβ+ cells expressing high levels of Zfp423 (GFP+ or Zfp423High) represent highly committed preadipocytes while Zfp423Low cells (GFP-) lacked significant adipogenic capacity, and exhibited significantly different global patterns of gene expression (Vishvanath et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: tSNE analysis of 1045 cell transcriptomes revealed distinct cell clusters exhibiting unique transcriptional profiles.
source: tSNE analysis of 1045 cell transcriptomes revealed distinct cell clusters exhibiting unique transcriptional profiles (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This statement describes the results of single-cell RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: Many of the top 20 most enriched transcripts in Cluster 1A and Cluster 1B correspond to notable genes related to adipogenesis and/or adipocyte gene expression.
source: Many of the top 20 most enriched transcripts in Cluster 1A and Cluster 1B correspond to notable genes related to adipogenesis and/or adipocyte gene expression (Figure 1D).
evidence: This statement describes the gene expression patterns observed in the scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The majority of cells in Clusters 1A and 1B express high levels of Pparg, Fabp4, Hsd11b1, and Lpl.
source: In particular, the majority of cells in Clusters 1A and 1B express high levels of Pparg, Fabp4, Hsd11b1, and Lpl, indicating these clusters may represent the PDGFRβ+ APC population within visceral WAT (Figure 1E).
evidence: This statement describes the gene expression patterns observed in the scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Cluster 1B enriches in the expression of Pparg, Cebpa, and other markers of terminal adipocyte differentiation, including Plin1, Fabp5, Car3, and Cd36.
source: Interestingly, Cluster 1B further enriches in the expression of Pparg, Cebpa, and other markers of terminal adipocyte differentiation, including Plin1, Fabp5, Car3, and Cd36 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This statement describes the gene expression patterns observed in the scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The expression of Adipoq, Retn, and Adrb3, genes typically characteristic of mature adipocytes, were detected within some cells within Cluster 1B.
source: Notably, the expression of Adipoq, Retn, and Adrb3, genes typically characteristic of mature adipocytes, were detected within some cells within Cluster 1B (Figure 1F).
evidence: This statement describes the gene expression patterns observed in the scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Cells of Cluster 1A/B enriched for gene sets related to 'adipogenesis'.
source: Unbiased gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that cells of Cluster 1A/B enriched for gene sets related to 'adipogenesis' and cells of Cluster 1B enriched for gene signatures of 'oxidative phosphorylation,' 'adipogenesis,' and fatty acid metabolism (Tables 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement describes the results of GSEA analysis shown in Tables 1 and 2.

claim: Cells of Cluster 1B enriched for gene signatures of 'oxidative phosphorylation,' 'adipogenesis,' and fatty acid metabolism.
source: Unbiased gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that cells of Cluster 1A/B enriched for gene sets related to 'adipogenesis' and cells of Cluster 1B enriched for gene signatures of 'oxidative phosphorylation,' 'adipogenesis,' and fatty acid metabolism (Tables 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement describes the results of GSEA analysis shown in Tables 1 and 2.

claim: Cluster 1A and 1B represent 'adipocyte precursor cells' (APCs), with Cluster 1B representing a subpopulation of APCs that are 'committed preadipocytes'.
source: These data suggest Cluster 1A and 1B represent 'adipocyte precursor cells' (APCs), with Cluster 1B representing a subpopulation of APCs that are 'committed preadipocytes'.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the gene expression data from scRNA-seq and GSEA.

claim: The cells in Cluster 2 were highly enriched in the expression of genes associated with fibrosis and inflammation, including Fn1, Loxl2, Tgfb2, and Ccl2.
source: The cells in Cluster 2 were highly enriched in the expression of genes associated with fibrosis and inflammation, including Fn1, Loxl2, Tgfb2, and Ccl2 (Figure 1D and G).
evidence: This statement describes the gene expression patterns observed in the scRNA-seq data shown in Figures 1D and 1G.

claim: GSEA revealed the enrichment of numerous gene signatures characteristic of a fibrogenic and inflammatory phenotype in Cluster 2, including gene sets corresponding to 'inflammatory response,' 'TGFβ signaling,' 'TNFα signaling,' and 'hypoxia'.
source: GSEA revealed the enrichment of numerous gene signatures characteristic of a fibrogenic and inflammatory phenotype, including gene sets corresponding to 'inflammatory response,' 'TGFβ signaling,' 'TNFα signaling,' and 'hypoxia' (Table 3).
evidence: This statement describes the results of GSEA analysis shown in Table 3.

claim: Cluster 3 had a mesothelial-like cell (herein, 'MLCs') expression profile.
source: Cluster 3 was molecularly quite distinct from Clusters 1A/B and 2. Interestingly, Cluster 3 had a mesothelial-like cell (herein, 'MLCs') expression profile.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the gene expression data from scRNA-seq.

claim: Mesothelial cells are epithelial cells of mesodermal origin that form a monolayer (mesothelium) lining the visceral serosa.
source: Mesothelial cells are epithelial cells of mesodermal origin that form a monolayer (mesothelium) lining the visceral serosa.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about mesothelial cells.

claim: Mesothelial cells and mural cells share a common developmental lineage.
source: Mesothelial cells and mural cells share a common developmental lineage.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about cell lineage relationships.

claim: Various stromal cell populations within visceral tissues, including APCs, descend from embryonic mesothelial cells.
source: Multiple genetic lineage tracing studies in mice indicate that various stromal cell populations within visceral tissues, including APCs, descend from embryonic mesothelial cells (Chau et al., 2014; Rinkevich et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mesothelial cells have been linked to multiple aspects of adipose tissue development and remodeling, including adipogenesis and inflammation.
source: Mesothelial cells have been linked to multiple aspects of adipose tissue development and remodeling, including adipogenesis and inflammation (Darimont et al., 2008; Gupta and Gupta, 2015; Mutsaers et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Cluster 3 was enriched for genes representing common mesothelial/epithelial markers, such as Msln, Upk3b, Krt8, and Krt14.
source: Cluster 3 was enriched for genes representing common mesothelial/epithelial markers, such as Msln, Upk3b, Krt8, and Krt14 (Figure 1D and H).
evidence: This statement describes the gene expression patterns observed in the scRNA-seq data shown in Figures 1D and 1H.

claim: The PdgfrbrtTA transgene targets at least a subset of visceral WAT associated mesothelial cells.
source: The presence of this cluster suggested that the PdgfrbrtTA transgene targets at least a subset of visceral WAT associated mesothelial cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the presence of mesothelial markers in Cluster 3 and confirmed by imaging data.

claim: Following transient doxycycline treatment of MuralChaser mice, a few mGFP+ cells can be observed within in the outermost epithelial layer of gonadal WAT.
source: Indeed, following transient doxycycline treatment of MuralChaser mice, a few mGFP+ cells can be observed within in the outermost epithelial layer of gonadal WAT (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This statement describes imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: mGFP+ cells can be occasionally observed within cultures of isolated mesothelial cells obtained from gWAT of doxycycline-treated MuralChaser mice.
source: Moreover, mGFP+ cells can be occasionally observed within cultures of isolated mesothelial cells obtained from gWAT of doxycycline-treated MuralChaser mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This statement describes imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Ly6c1 expression was abundant in FIPs but not APCs.
source: Of note, Ly6c1 expression was abundant in FIPs but not APCs (Figure 2B).
evidence: This statement describes the gene expression patterns observed in the scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The expression of Cd9 was abundantly expressed in both the FIPs and MLCs.
source: The expression of Cd9, a recently described marker of fibrogenic cells (Marcelin et al., 2017), was abundantly expressed in both the FIPs and MLCs (Figure 2B).
evidence: This statement describes the gene expression patterns observed in the scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Three distinct subpopulations of PDGFRβ+ cells were apparent: LY6C- CD9- (APCs), LY6C+ (FIPs), and LY6C- CD9+ (MLCs) cells.
source: Three distinct subpopulations of PDGFRβ+ cells were apparent: LY6C- CD9- (APCs), LY6C+ (FIPs), and LY6C- CD9+ (MLCs) cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: This statement describes the FACS gating strategy shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Flow cytometry analysis consistently revealed that LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells were more abundant than LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells and Ly6C- CD9+ PDGFRβ+ cells.
source: Flow cytometry analysis consistently revealed that LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells were more abundant than LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells and Ly6C- CD9+ PDGFRβ+ cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: This statement describes the flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Gene expression analysis by qPCR revealed that LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells were enriched in the expression of genes that defined the APC population (Cluster 1).
source: Importantly, gene expression analysis by qPCR revealed that LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells were enriched in the expression of genes that defined the APC population (Cluster 1) (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells enriched for the mRNAs that initially defined the FIPs (Cluster 2).
source: LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells enriched for the mRNAs that initially defined the FIPs (Cluster 2) (Figure 2E,G)
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figures 2E and 2G.

claim: LY6C- CD9+ PDGFRβ+ cells expressed the mesothelial/epithelial markers that defined Cluster 3.
source: and LY6C- CD9+ PDGFRβ+ cells expressed the mesothelial/epithelial markers that defined Cluster 3 (Figure 2E,H).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figures 2E and 2H.

claim: Freshly sorted LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells are enriched in Pparg expression when compared to LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells.
source: Indeed, freshly sorted LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells are enriched in Pparg expression when compared to LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells proliferate at a greater rate than LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells.
source: Under these growth conditions, LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells proliferate at a greater rate than LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells; however, the two subpopulations appear morphologically indistinguishable, with both populations appearing fibroblast-like until reaching confluence (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C,E).
evidence: This statement describes the in vitro proliferation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: LY6C- CD9+ PDGFRβ+ cells (MLCs) grow to confluence and adopt a cobblestone-like morphology characteristic of cultured mesothelial cells.
source: LY6C- CD9+ PDGFRβ+ cells (MLCs) grow to confluence and adopt a cobblestone-like morphology characteristic of cultured mesothelial cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This statement describes the morphological observations shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Upon reaching confluence, only LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells (APCs) underwent spontaneous adipocyte differentiation at a high efficiency.
source: Remarkably, upon reaching confluence, only LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells (APCs) underwent spontaneous adipocyte differentiation at a high efficiency, while very few adipocytes emerged in the other two PDGFRβ+ subpopulations or within cultures containing all PDGFRβ+ cells from gWAT (Figure 3).
evidence: This statement describes the in vitro differentiation data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Confluent cultures of LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells stimulated with a hormonal adipogenic cocktail (dexamethasone, IBMX, insulin, and PPARγ agonist, Rosiglitazone) underwent adipocyte differentiation to some degree.
source: Confluent cultures of LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells stimulated with a more commonly used hormonal adipogenic cocktail (dexamethasone, IBMX, insulin, and PPARγ agonist, Rosiglitazone) underwent to adipocyte differentiation to some degree (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement describes the in vitro differentiation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells still did not differentiate to the same extent as LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells stimulated with insulin alone, despite strong adipogenic stimulus.
source: Despite this strong adipogenic stimulus, LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells still did not differentiate to the same extent as LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells stimulated with insulin alone (see Figure 3).
evidence: This statement compares the differentiation capacity shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: 3 weeks following cell transplantation, the WAT depots of all four animals injected with LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells contain numerous clusters of lipid-laden fat cells.
source: 3 weeks following cell transplantation, the WAT depots all four animals injected with LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells contain numerous clusters of lipid-laden fat cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This statement describes the in vivo transplantation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The contralateral depots of the same animals injected with LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells, or matrigel alone, remained devoid of adipocytes.
source: The contralateral depots of the same animals injected with LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells, or matrigel alone, remained devoid of adipocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C,D).
evidence: This statement describes the in vivo transplantation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C,D.

claim: LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells are highly adipogenic functional gonadal white adipocyte precursors.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells are highly adipogenic functional gonadal white adipocyte precursors, while LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells are largely refractory to adipogenic stimuli.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vitro and in vivo differentiation data.

claim: LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells are largely refractory to adipogenic stimuli.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells are highly adipogenic functional gonadal white adipocyte precursors, while LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells are largely refractory to adipogenic stimuli.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vitro and in vivo differentiation data.

claim: APCs from gonadal WAT have been defined as SCA-1+ CD34+ CD24± cells that also express PDGFRα.
source: Several studies have defined APCs from gonadal WAT as SCA-1+ CD34+ CD24± cells that also express PDGFRα (Berry and Rodeheffer, 2013; Jeffery et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2012; Rodeheffer et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: All three PDGFRβ+ subpopulations expressed Pdgfra, Ly6a (SCA-1), and Cd34.
source: The scRNA-seq analysis and follow-up qPCR analyses of isolated subpopulations revealed that all three PDGFRβ+ subpopulations indeed expressed Pdgfra, Ly6a (SCA-1), and Cd34
evidence: This statement describes the gene expression data from scRNA-seq and qPCR.

claim: The mRNA levels of Ly6a and Cd34 are lower in LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ APCs than in LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells (FIPs).
source: however, the mRNA levels of Ly6a and Cd34 are actually lower in LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ APCs than in LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells (FIPs) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F,G.

claim: All three subpopulations expressed Pdgfrb; however, mRNA levels of Pdgfrb were quantitatively lower in FIPs than in the APCs and MLCs.
source: As expected, all three subpopulations expressed Pdgfrb; however, mRNA levels of Pdgfrb were quantitatively lower in FIPs than in the APCs and MLCs.
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data.

claim: Levels of Cd24a were low in all three PDGFRβ+ subpopulations.
source: qPCR analysis indicated that levels of Cd24a were low in all three PDGFRβ+ subpopulations.
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data.

claim: Cd38 was present predominately in LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells.
source: Cd38 was present predominately in LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells, consistent with the notion that CD38 identifies APCs from this depot (Carrière et al., 2017) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F,G and is supported by a citation.

claim: The selection of gonadal WAT SVF cells on the basis of SCA-1/CD34 yields functionally heterogeneous cell populations.
source: Collectively, these data reveal the selection of gonadal WAT SVF cells on the basis of SCA-1/CD34 yields functionally heterogeneous cell populations, and perhaps biases against the selection of LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ APCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gene expression and functional data.

claim: Burl et al. identified two prominent populations within the gonadal WAT depot, termed adipose stem cell (ASC) 1 and ASC 2.
source: Recently, Burl et al. reported scRNA-seq profiles of adipose SVF cells, creating a cellular atlas of potential adipocyte precursor populations (perivascular and non-perivascular) (Burl et al., 2018). Notably, the authors identified two prominent populations within the gonadal WAT depot, termed adipose stem cell (ASC) 1 and ASC 2.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: ASC 1 defined by Burl et al. bears close resemblance to the APC population defined in this study.
source: The identified populations were not isolated and explored functionally in their study; however, a comparison of the molecular profiles strongly suggests that ASC 1 defined by the authors bears close resemblance to APC population defined in our study, while the ASC 2 population bears close resemblance to the FIPs discovered here (Figure 3—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is a comparison of molecular profiles shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1I.

claim: ASC 2 defined by Burl et al. bears close resemblance to the FIPs discovered in this study.
source: The identified populations were not isolated and explored functionally in their study; however, a comparison of the molecular profiles strongly suggests that ASC 1 defined by the authors bears close resemblance to APC population defined in our study, while the ASC 2 population bears close resemblance to the FIPs discovered here (Figure 3—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is a comparison of molecular profiles shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1I.

claim: Gonadal WAT PDGFRβ+ cells expressing GFP are enriched in the expression of Pparg and are highly adipogenic in vitro.
source: Our prior studies of Zfp423GFP reporter mice indicated that gonadal WAT PDGFRβ+ cells expressing GFP are enriched in the expression of Pparg and are highly adipogenic in vitro (Gupta et al., 2012; Vishvanath et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: Zfp423GFP reporter captures committed preadipocytes within the skeletal bone marrow microenvironment.
source: Additional studies by others indicated that this reporter captures committed preadipocytes within the skeletal bone marrow microenvironment (Ambrosi et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Endogenous Zfp423 mRNA levels were found in all PDGFRβ+ subpopulations, albeit at highest levels in APCs.
source: Endogenous Zfp423 mRNA levels were found in all PDGFRβ+ subpopulations, albeit at highest levels in APCs. (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Zfp423GFP-High PDGFRβ+ cells were enriched in the expression of Pparg isoforms when compared to Zfp423GFP-Low PDGFRβ+ cells.
source: Consistent with our prior studies, Zfp423GFP-High PDGFRβ+ cells were enriched in the expression of Pparg isoforms when compared to Zfp423GFP-Low PDGFRβ+ cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4C.

claim: Zfp423GFP-High cells were enriched in the expression of the genes that define the APC clusters, but not FIPs or MLCs.
source: Further gene expression analysis of the top cluster gene markers revealed that Zfp423GFP-High cells were enriched in the expression of the genes that define the APC clusters, but not FIPs or MLCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 4D–G).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4D–G.

claim: Zfp423GFP-High PDGFRβ+ cells were enriched in the expression of genes that delineate the more committed preadipocytes cluster (Cluster 1B) identified by scRNA-seq.
source: In particular, Zfp423GFP-High PDGFRβ+ cells were enriched in the expression of genes that delineate the more committed preadipocytes cluster (Cluster 1B) identified by scRNA-seq (Figure 3—figure supplement 4E).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4E.

claim: Endogenous Zfp423 mRNA expression is not confined exclusively to the APC subpopulation of PDGFRβ+ cells in gWAT.
source: Taken all together, these data indicate that endogenous Zfp423 mRNA expression is not confined exclusively to the APC subpopulation of PDGFRβ+ cells in gWAT; however, Zfp423GFP reporter mice represent a genetic tool to localize and enrich for committed preadipocytes from this depot.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gene expression data.

claim: Zfp423GFP reporter mice represent a genetic tool to localize and enrich for committed preadipocytes from gonadal WAT.
source: Taken all together, these data indicate that endogenous Zfp423 mRNA expression is not confined exclusively to the APC subpopulation of PDGFRβ+ cells in gWAT; however, Zfp423GFP reporter mice represent a genetic tool to localize and enrich for committed preadipocytes from this depot.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gene expression data.

claim: The same three populations can be observed within the mesenteric and retroperitoneal depots of adult male mice, with LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells representing the highly adipogenic subpopulation.
source: Indeed, the same three populations can be observed within the mesenteric and retroperitoneal depots of adult male mice, with LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells representing the highly adipogenic subpopulation (Figure 4A–H).
evidence: This statement describes the FACS and differentiation data shown in Figure 4A–H.

claim: All PDGFRβ+ cells within the inguinal and anterior subcutaneous WAT depots expressed LY6C.
source: We also examined LY6C expression within PDGFRβ+ SVF cells obtained from the inguinal and anterior subcutaneous WAT depots. We previously demonstrated that the total pool of PDGFRβ+ cells from inguinal WAT is very highly adipogenic in vitro (Shao et al., 2018); however, remarkably, all PDGFRβ+ cells within the inguinal and anterior subcutaneous WAT depots expressed LY6C (Figure 4I).
evidence: This statement describes the FACS data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Functionally distinct perivascular cell subpopulations from visceral, but not subcutaneous, WAT depots can be revealed on the basis of LY6C and CD9 expression.
source: Therefore, functionally distinct perivascular cell subpopulations from visceral, but not subcutaneous, WAT depots can be revealed on the basis of LY6C and CD9 expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the FACS and functional data.

claim: Within the SVF of peri-ovarian WAT, the same three distinct subpopulations of PDGFRβ+ cells can be discriminated, with FIPs being the predominant population.
source: Within the SVF of peri-ovarian WAT, the same three distinct subpopulations of PDGFRβ+ cells can be discriminated, with FIPs being the predominant population (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This statement describes the FACS data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells from peri-ovarian WAT are functional adipocyte precursors; these cells, but neither FIPs nor MLCs, differentiate spontaneously upon reaching confluence in culture.
source: Moreover, LY6C- CD9- PDGFRβ+ cells from peri-ovarian WAT are functional adipocyte precursors; these cells, but neither FIPs nor MLCs, differentiate spontaneously upon reaching confluence in culture (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I–K).
evidence: This statement describes the in vitro differentiation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1I–K.

claim: Functional APCs from both male and female visceral WAT can be isolated through this cell sorting strategy.
source: Collectively, these data provide evidence that functional APCs from both male and female visceral WAT can be isolated through this cell sorting strategy.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the functional data from multiple depots and sexes.

claim: Very little spontaneous adipocyte differentiation occurs in cultures containing the total pool of visceral adipose PDGFRβ+ cells, despite the presence of numerous APCs within this population.
source: It is notable that very little spontaneous adipocyte differentiation occurs in cultures containing the total pool of visceral adipose PDGFRβ+ cells (Figure 3A,E,I,M,Q), despite the presence of numerous APCs within this population.
evidence: This statement describes the in vitro differentiation data shown in Figure 3.

claim: APCs exposed to conditioned media from FIPs, but not from parallel cultures of APCs, expressed lower levels of Pparg.
source: Remarkably, APCs exposed to conditioned media from FIPs, but not from parallel cultures of APCs, expressed lower levels of Pparg (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data from conditioned media experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: APCs exposed to conditioned media from FIPs lost a significant degree of adipogenic capacity.
source: Moreover, APCs exposed to conditioned media from FIPs lost a significant degree of adipogenic capacity (Figure 5B,C,E).
evidence: This statement describes the in vitro differentiation data from conditioned media experiments shown in Figure 5B,C,E.

claim: Conditioned media from cultures of MLCs had only a slight inhibitory effect on the terminal differentiation of APCs.
source: Conditioned media from cultures of MLCs had only a slight inhibitory effect on the terminal differentiation of APCs (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This statement describes the in vitro differentiation data from conditioned media experiments shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: FIPs can be anti-adipogenic.
source: Collectively, these data not only suggest that FIPs lack significant adipogenic capacity, but highlight the notion that these cells can actually be anti-adipogenic.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the conditioned media experiments.

claim: Schwalie et al. identified anti-adipogenic stromal cells within the inguinal WAT of mice, termed Aregs, which are defined, in part, by the expression of CD142 and ABCG1 and exhibit perivascular localization.
source: Recently, Schwalie et al. identified anti-adipogenic stromal cells within the inguinal WAT of mice (Schwalie et al., 2018). These cells, termed Aregs, are defined, in part, by the expression of CD142 and ABCG1 and exhibit perivascular localization.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: F3 expression (encoding CD142) is detected in all PDGFRβ+ clusters of gonadal WAT, albeit not enriched in FIPs.
source: From our scRNA-seq dataset, we observed that F3 expression (encoding CD142) is detected in all PDGFRβ+ clusters of gonadal WAT, albeit not enriched in FIPs (Figure 5F).
evidence: This statement describes the scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Abcg1 expression was not detected by the sequencing analysis in any PDGFRβ+ population.
source: Abcg1 expression was not detected by the sequencing analysis in any population.
evidence: This statement describes the scRNA-seq data.

claim: Neither F3 nor Abcg1 was enriched in FIPs by qPCR analysis.
source: We also examined the levels of mRNA for these two markers directly by quantitative PCR analysis. Consistent with the sequencing data, neither marker was enriched in FIPs (Figure 5G).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: There was no selective enrichment of the broader set of Areg markers within FIPs or APCs.
source: We also examined additional genes (23 in total) whose expression defines Aregs, as identified by Schwalie et al, by assessing their expression level within our scRNA-seq dataset (Figure 5H). Levels of transcripts corresponding to a number of these genes were detectable, albeit at low levels. Notably, there was no selective enrichment of the broader set of Areg markers within FIPs or APCs.
evidence: This statement describes the analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Despite some shared functional similarities, inguinal adipose Aregs and the gonadal adipose FIPs described here appear molecularly distinct.
source: As such, despite some shared functional similarities, inguinal adipose Aregs and the gonadal adipose FIPs described here appear molecularly distinct.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of gene expression profiles.

claim: The expression of major collagens (Col1a1 and Col3a1) and some of the assayed genes associated with extracellular matrix accumulation were enriched in freshly isolated LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells compared to the other PDGFRβ+ subpopulations.
source: Indeed the expression of major collagens (Col1a1 and Col3a1) and some of the assayed genes associated with extracellular matrix accumulation were enriched in freshly isolated LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ cells compared to the other PDGFRβ+ subpopulations (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cultured FIPs and APCs were both responsive to treatment with recombinant TGFβ; however, the expression of collagens examined remained higher and/or was further induced in FIPs.
source: In vitro, cultured FIPs and APCs were both responsive to treatment with recombinant TGFβ; however, the expression of collagens examined remained higher and/or was further induced in FIPs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data from TGFβ treatment experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ FIPs exhibit a phenotype characteristic of fibrogenic cells.
source: These data indicate that LY6C+ PDGFRβ+ FIPs exhibit a phenotype characteristic of fibrogenic cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gene expression and TGFβ response data.

claim: FIPs exhibited a robust inflammatory gene expression signature following acute exposure to pro-inflammatory molecules.
source: Remarkably, FIPs exhibited a robust inflammatory gene expression signature following acute exposure to pro-inflammatory molecules.
evidence: This is a summary of the inflammatory response data.

claim: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) treatment induced inflammatory cytokine gene expression in both APCs and FIPs; however, the response was more robust in the latter population.
source: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) treatment induced inflammatory cytokine gene expression in both APCs and FIPs; however, the response was more robust in the latter population (Figure 6A).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data from LPS treatment experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: FIPs, but not APCs, activate the expression of several pro-inflammatory cytokines under TNFα treatment conditions.
source: The differential response to TNFα treatment was the most striking; FIPs, but not APCs, activate the expression of several pro-inflammatory cytokines under these conditions (Figure 6B).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data from TNFα treatment experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Macrophage cultures exposed to conditioned media from LPS-treated FIPs had the most robust induction of pro-inflammatory genes, including Tnfα, Il1β, and Il6.
source: Macrophage cultures exposed to conditioned media from LPS-treated FIPs had the most robust induction of pro-inflammatory genes, including Tnfα, Il1β, and Il6 (Figure 6D).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data from macrophage activation experiments shown in Figure 6D.

claim: FIPs have the potential to exert a functional pro-inflammatory phenotype.
source: These data highlight the potential for FIPs to exert a functional pro-inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the inflammatory response and macrophage activation data.

claim: Four weeks of HFD feeding did not appear to dramatically alter the absolute number of PDGFRβ+ cells present in gWAT.
source: Four weeks of HFD feeding did not appear to dramatically alter the absolute number of PDGFRβ+ cells present in gWAT; however, the ratio of FIPs to APCs begins to increase by as early as one week of HFD feeding (Figure 7A).
evidence: This statement describes the FACS data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The ratio of FIPs to APCs begins to increase by as early as one week of HFD feeding.
source: Four weeks of HFD feeding did not appear to dramatically alter the absolute number of PDGFRβ+ cells present in gWAT; however, the ratio of FIPs to APCs begins to increase by as early as one week of HFD feeding (Figure 7A).
evidence: This statement describes the FACS data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: FIPs and the MLCs displayed the greatest BrdU incorporation during one week of HFD feeding.
source: We also analyzed BrdU incorporation into the mural cell populations during one week of HFD feeding. FIPs and the MLCs displayed the greatest BrdU incorporation (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This statement describes the BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 7B,C.

claim: BrdU incorporation into APCs was significantly lower than observed in the FIPs.
source: BrdU incorporation into APCs was significantly lower than observed in the FIPs (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This statement describes the BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 7B,C.

claim: Frequencies of APCs and FIPs are differentially regulated in vivo in association with high-fat diet feeding, with FIPs exhibiting a relatively higher degree of cell proliferation under these conditions.
source: These data indicate that frequencies of APCs and FIPs are differentially regulated in vivo in association with high-fat diet feeding, with FIPs exhibiting a relatively higher degree of cell proliferation under these conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the FACS and BrdU incorporation data.

claim: One month of HFD feeding lead to a significant elevation in mRNA levels of Pparg isoform two expression in APCs, with a smaller increase occurring in MLCs.
source: One month of HFD feeding lead to a significant elevation in mRNA levels of Pparg isoform two expression in APCs, with a smaller increase occurring in MLCs (Figure 7D).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Pparg isoform two expression was not elevated in FIPs following HFD feeding.
source: Pparg isoform two expression was not elevated in FIPs, consistent with their apparent lack of adipogenic potential (Figure 7D).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: mRNA levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and extracellular matrix components were further induced and/or remained more abundant in FIPs than in APCs or MLCs following HFD feeding.
source: mRNA levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and extracellular matrix components were further induced and/or remained more abundant in FIPs than in APCs or MLCs (Figure 7E–M).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 7E–M.

claim: APCs activated the expression of some inflammatory and fibrogenic genes (e.g. Il6, Tnfa, Col1a1, Col3a1) during HFD feeding.
source: Interestingly, APCs activated the expression of some of these genes (e.g. Il6, Tnfa, Col1a1, Col3a1) during HFD feeding.
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data.

claim: APCs have some capacity to adopt characteristics of FIPs in vivo.
source: These data are consistent with the in vitro analyses highlighting the potential of APCs to trigger some degree of an inflammatory response in pro-inflammatory stimuli (see Figure 6). These data reveal that PDGFRβ+ subpopulations exhibit unique transcriptional responses to HFD feeding; however, these data also suggest that APCs have some capacity to adopt characteristics of FIPs in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gene expression data following HFD feeding.

claim: The expression of all three members of the Nr4a family of nuclear hormone receptors was significantly enriched in the FIPs cluster.
source: A number of transcription factors were differentially expressed between FIPs and APCs; however, it was notable that the expression of all three members of the Nr4a family of nuclear hormone receptors was significantly enriched in the FIPs cluster (Figure 8A).
evidence: This statement describes the scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Gene expression analysis by qPCR confirmed the significant enrichment of Nr4a1, Nr4a2, and Nr4a3 in FIPs isolated from chow-fed mice, with relatively lower expression in the APCs and MLCs.
source: Gene expression analysis by qPCR of the isolated populations confirmed the significant enrichment of Nr4a1, Nr4a2, and Nr4a3 in FIPs isolated from chow-fed mice, with relatively lower expression in the APCs and MLCs (Figure 8B).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Following 4 weeks of HFD-feeding, the expression of Nr4a family members remained significantly enriched in FIPs.
source: Following 4 weeks of HFD-feeding, the expression of Nr4a family members remained significantly enriched in FIPs (Figure 8C).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The expression of all Nr4a family members in FIPs was increased following exposure to recombinant TNFα in vitro.
source: In vitro, the expression of all Nr4a family members in FIPs was increased following exposure to recombinant TNFα (Figure 8D).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Overexpression of Nr4a1, Nr4a2, or Nr4a3, attenuated the pro-inflammatory response to TNFα in FIPs.
source: Overexpression of Nr4a1, Nr4a2, or Nr4a3, attenuated the pro-inflammatory response to TNFα (Figure 8H–K).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data from overexpression experiments shown in Figure 8H–K.

claim: Knockdown of Nr4a1 using three independent shRNAs led to an exaggerated response of FIPs to TNFα treatment.
source: Moreover, we assessed the impact of retroviral-mediated knockdown of Nr4a1 on the inflammatory response in FIPs. Knockdown of Nr4a1 using three independent shRNAs led to an exaggerated response of FIPs to TNFα treatment (Figure 8L–P).
evidence: This statement describes the qPCR data from knockdown experiments shown in Figure 8L–P.

claim: FIPs activate Nr4a family members in response to pro-inflammatory stimuli, perhaps as a means to counter-regulate a sustained cellular inflammatory response.
source: These gain- and loss of function studies suggest that FIPs activate Nr4a family members in response to pro-inflammatory stimuli, perhaps as a means to counter-regulate a sustained cellular inflammatory response.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gain- and loss-of-function experiments.
